ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What label marks the bundle sheath cell in the diagram?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a structural schematic diagram of a leaf cross section, with multiple letter labels and arrows on the right side. At the middle-right position there is a group of brown stacked tubular tissues, surrounded on the outside by a ring of light-blue cells. The arrow of label E points to one of the cells in this ring of light-blue cells; the bracket of label A marks the entire vascular bundle region. Reasoning: The characteristic of bundle sheath cells is that they surround the leaf vein or vascular bundle to form a ring of sheath-like structure. The ring of light-blue cells surrounding the brown vascular tissue in the figure matches the position and morphology of bundle sheath cells, and the label pointing to this cell is E. Therefore, the bundle sheath cell is labeled by E.
